$$
\int_C x - 2 y\,\mathrm{d}s=\sqrt{10}\int_{0}^{4}\boxed{}\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

where $C$ is the segment of the line $\frac{x}{4}=1 - \frac{3 y}{4}$ traversed between the points $(4,0)$ and $(-8,4)$. Which of the following is the missing expression under the integral on the right?

*Hint: Use the parameter $y=t.$*" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the given curve can be expressed in the form $x=x(y),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{x}{4}=1 - \frac{3 y}{4}\,\Longrightarrow\,x=4 - 3 y
$$

Therefore, by setting $y=t,$ we have 

$$
x=x(t)=4 - 3 t.
$$

 

This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle 4 - 3 t,\,t\rangle,\quad 0\le t\le 4
$$

Note that the domain $0\le t\le 4$ is defined by the $y$-coordinates of the end-points on the path.

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(4 - 3 t)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)j \\ &=(-3)i+j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(-3)^2+1^2} \\ &=\sqrt{9+1} \\ &=\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=x - 2 y,$ then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=1\left(4 - 3 t\right)-2t \\ &=4 - 5 t.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C x - 2 y\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{0}^{4}f(r(t))\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{4}(4 - 5 t)\cdot \sqrt{10}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\sqrt{10}\int_{0}^{4}(4 - 5 t)\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["6ee0746c-4281-5a79-87b4-bd2fbd506c40"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "e0c023e8-5a47-5179-b7eb-afe7ce12e7ed" :answer/id #uuid "e0c023e8-5a47-5179-b7eb-afe7ce12e7ed" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4 t^{3} \left(2 t + 2\right)^{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "b7a2acf9-a41f-5160-8dc1-756db6ef76d6" :answer/id #uuid "b7a2acf9-a41f-5160-8dc1-756db6ef76d6" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "16 t^{5}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "4ce1b2b9-3b87-52e0-a1f6-172a88bf7b1f" :answer/id #uuid "4ce1b2b9-3b87-52e0-a1f6-172a88bf7b1f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4 t^{3} \left(2 - 2 t\right)^{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "f3bd6f10-f9f4-538e-913c-d22618c6f106" :answer/id #uuid "f3bd6f10-f9f4-538e-913c-d22618c6f106" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4 t^{2} \left(2 t + 2\right)^{3}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "680810eb-e33e-5d7a-ac2d-3e3d2bcc7f23" :answer/id #uuid "680810eb-e33e-5d7a-ac2d-3e3d2bcc7f23" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "4 \left(2 t + 2\right)^{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "4ecb885d-e56e-5e60-9407-9e9e3fa26bfa" :answer-field/id #uuid "4ecb885d-e56e-5e60-9407-9e9e3fa26bfa" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["e0c023e8-5a47-5179-b7eb-afe7ce12e7ed" "b7a2acf9-a41f-5160-8dc1-756db6ef76d6" "4ce1b2b9-3b87-52e0-a1f6-172a88bf7b1f" "f3bd6f10-f9f4-538e-913c-d22618c6f106" "680810eb-e33e-5d7a-ac2d-3e3d2bcc7f23"] :answer-field/correct "e0c023e8-5a47-5179-b7eb-afe7ce12e7ed" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "86be1e77-b581-5d25-9650-3cc553d658e6" :question/id #uuid "86be1e77-b581-5d25-9650-3cc553d658e6" :question/problem "Consider the line integral

$$

$$

where $C$ is the segment of the line $x=2 y + 2$ traversed between the points $(6,2)$ and $(10,4)$. Which of the following is the missing expression under the integral on the right?

*Hint: Use the parameter $y=t.$*" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the given curve is of the form $x=x(y).$ Therefore, by setting $y=t,$ we have 

$$
x=x(t)=2 t + 2.
$$

This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle 2 t + 2,\,t\rangle,\quad 2\le t\le 4
$$

Note that the domain $2\le t\le 4$ is defined by the $y$-coordinates of the end-points on the path.

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 t + 2)i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)j \\ &=(2)i+j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(2)^2+1^2} \\ &=\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if $f(x,y)=4 x^{2} y^{3},$ then we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=4\left(2 t + 2\right)^{2}t^{3} \\ &=4 t^{3} \left(2 t + 2\right)^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C 4 x^{2} y^{3}\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{2}^{4}f(r(t))\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{2}^{4}(4 t^{3} \left(2 t + 2\right)^{2})\cdot \sqrt{5}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\sqrt{5}\int_{2}^{4}4 t^{3} \left(2 t + 2\right)^{2}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["4ecb885d-e56e-5e60-9407-9e9e3fa26bfa"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "7aee2490-8ebd-5fff-aeba-dd54ccd94877" :answer/id #uuid "7aee2490-8ebd-5fff-aeba-dd54ccd94877" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3 t^{5}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "ac98de36-83ed-5aef-b75d-338dc0b2dbdf" :answer/id #uuid "ac98de36-83ed-5aef-b75d-338dc0b2dbdf" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "768 t^{5}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "2275c2b9-bd7c-5d72-90c8-7b26275f195e" :answer/id #uuid "2275c2b9-bd7c-5d72-90c8-7b26275f195e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "12 t^{5}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "36e310df-bff1-5173-9e88-7181749cd810" :answer/id #uuid "36e310df-bff1-5173-9e88-7181749cd810" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\frac{3 t^{5}}{64}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "77b420d0-67c2-528a-91a7-5fcbbe514595" :answer/id #uuid "77b420d0-67c2-528a-91a7-5fcbbe514595" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3 t^{2}" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "e31bb3e8-a091-5beb-bbef-ce8a5745dea3" :answer-field/id #uuid "e31bb3e8-a091-5beb-bbef-ce8a5745dea3" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["7aee2490-8ebd-5fff-aeba-dd54ccd94877" "ac98de36-83ed-5aef-b75d-338dc0b2dbdf" "2275c2b9-bd7c-5d72-90c8-7b26275f195e" "36e310df-bff1-5173-9e88-7181749cd810" "77b420d0-67c2-528a-91a7-5fcbbe514595"] :answer-field/correct "7aee2490-8ebd-5fff-aeba-dd54ccd94877" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "4996d341-4274-5583-88ff-0f580b30aea8" :question/id #uuid "4996d341-4274-5583-88ff-0f580b30aea8" :question/problem "Consider the line integral

$$
\int_C 48 x^{2} y^{3}\,\mathrm{d}s=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}\int_{1}^{2}\boxed{}\,\mathrm{d}t
$$

where $C$ is the segment of the line $4x=y$ traversed between the points $(\frac{1}{4},1)$ and $(\frac{1}{2},2)$. Which of the following is the missing expression under the integral on the right?

*Hint: Use the parameter $y=t.$*" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the given curve can be expressed in the form $x=x(y),$ as follows:

$$
4x=y\,\Longrightarrow\,x=\frac{y}{4}
$$

Therefore, by setting $y=t,$ we have 

$$
x=x(t)=\frac{t}{4}.
$$

 

This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle\frac{t}{4},\,t\rangle,\quad 1\le t\le 2
$$

Note that the domain $1\le t\le 2$ is defined by the $y$-coordinates of the end-points on the path.

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(\frac{t}{4})i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)j \\ &=(\frac{1}{4})i+j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(\frac{1}{4})^2+1^2} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{1}{16}+1} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{17}{16}} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=48 x^{2} y^{3},$ then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=48\left(\frac{t}{4}\right)^2t^{3} \\ &=48\left(\frac{t^2}{16}\right)t^{3} \\ &=3 t^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C 48 x^{2} y^{3}\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{1}^{2}f(r(t))\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{2}(3 t^{5})\cdot \frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{17}}{4}\int_{1}^{2}3 t^{5}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["e31bb3e8-a091-5beb-bbef-ce8a5745dea3"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "c7400a6a-8f3d-57bb-bce2-f39b5a9cf40c" :answer/id #uuid "c7400a6a-8f3d-57bb-bce2-f39b5a9cf40c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{1}^{e^{2}}t^{4} \sqrt{t^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "a0a0976d-6042-5f97-9145-cb3e806a614e" :answer/id #uuid "a0a0976d-6042-5f97-9145-cb3e806a614e" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{1}^{e^{2}}\sqrt{10} t^{5}\,\mathrm{d}t" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "05820e9b-5d3f-5f00-8ab1-5cb728ad058c" :answer/id #uuid "05820e9b-5d3f-5f00-8ab1-5cb728ad058c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{1}^{e^{2}}t \sqrt{t^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "3912c436-323c-5514-82b7-0a551fe02d0b" :answer/id #uuid "3912c436-323c-5514-82b7-0a551fe02d0b" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{1}^{e^{2}}t^{5} \sqrt{t^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "5534bb00-f895-5c7c-97e6-684d212578d9" :answer/id #uuid "5534bb00-f895-5c7c-97e6-684d212578d9" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "\int_{0}^{6}t^{4} \sqrt{t^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "2ae4cf2f-2882-5737-907d-832d0c62119c" :answer-field/id #uuid "2ae4cf2f-2882-5737-907d-832d0c62119c" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["c7400a6a-8f3d-57bb-bce2-f39b5a9cf40c" "a0a0976d-6042-5f97-9145-cb3e806a614e" "05820e9b-5d3f-5f00-8ab1-5cb728ad058c" "3912c436-323c-5514-82b7-0a551fe02d0b" "5534bb00-f895-5c7c-97e6-684d212578d9"] :answer-field/correct "c7400a6a-8f3d-57bb-bce2-f39b5a9cf40c" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "aa8602a5-ab99-5ec1-a115-7e29b5ef7be8" :question/id #uuid "aa8602a5-ab99-5ec1-a115-7e29b5ef7be8" :question/problem "Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $\int_C y^{2} e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}s$

where $C$ is the section of the curve $x=3 \ln{\left(y \right)}$ traversed between the points $(0,1)$ and $(6,e^{2})$.

*Hint: Use the parameter $y=t.$*" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the given curve is of the form $x=x(y).$ Therefore, by setting $y=t,$ we have 

$$
x=x(t)=3 \ln{\left(t \right)}.
$$

 

This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle 3 \ln{\left(t \right)},\,t\rangle,\quad 1\le t\le e^{2}
$$

Note that the domain $1\le t\le e^{2}$ is defined by the $y$-coordinates of the end-points on the path.

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(3 \ln{\left(t \right)})i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)j \\ &=(\frac{3}{t})i+j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(\frac{3}{t})^2+1^2} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{9}{t^2}+1} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{t^{2} + 9}{t^2}} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{t^{2} + 9}}{|t|} \\ &=\frac{\sqrt{t^{2} + 9}}{t}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=y^{2} e^{x},$ then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=1\left(e^{3\ln t}\right)t^{2} \\ &=1\left(t^{3}\right)t^{2} \\ &=t^{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int_C y^{2} e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}s&=\int_{1}^{e^{2}}f(r(t))\|r^{\prime}(t)\|\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{e^{2}}(t^{5})\cdot \sqrt{1 + \frac{9}{t^{2}}}\,\mathrm{d}t \\ &=\int_{1}^{e^{2}}t^{4} \sqrt{t^{2} + 9}\,\mathrm{d}t.\end{aligned}

"Which of the following is equivalent to the integral $\int_C 4 y e^{x}\,\mathrm{d}s$

where $C$ is the section of the curve $\frac{x}{2}=\ln y$ traversed between the points $(0,1)$ and $(4,e^{2})$.

*Hint: Use the parameter $y=t.$*" :question/worked-solution "Notice that the given curve can be expressed in the form $x=x(y),$ as follows:

$$
\frac{x}{2}=\ln y\,\Longrightarrow\,x=2 \ln{\left(y \right)}
$$

Therefore, by setting $y=t,$ we have 

$$
x=x(t)=2 \ln{\left(t \right)}.
$$

 

This gives the following parametrization of the curve:

$$
r(t)=\langle 2 \ln{\left(t \right)},\,t\rangle,\quad 1\le t\le e^{2}
$$

Note that the domain $1\le t\le e^{2}$ is defined by the $y$-coordinates of the end-points on the path.

Computing ${r}^{′}(t)$ and $‖{r}^{′}(t)‖,$ we get the following: 

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t)&=\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t}i+\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t}j \\ &=\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(2 \ln{\left(t \right)})i+\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}(t)j \\ &=(\frac{2}{t})i+j \\ \|r^{\prime}(t)\|&=\sqrt{(\frac{\mathrm{d}x}{\mathrm{d}t})^2+(\frac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t})^2} \\ &=\sqrt{(\frac{2}{t})^2+1^2} \\ &=\sqrt{\frac{4}{t^2}+1} \\ &=\frac{1}{t}\sqrt{t^{2} + 4}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, if  $f(x,y)=4 y e^{x}$, then we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}f(r(t))&=4 y e^{x} \\ &=4\cdot t^{1}e^{2\ln t} \\ &=4\cdot t^{1}\left(t^{2}\right) \\ &=4 t^{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we can write the integral as
